{
  "answer": "1) Difficulty classifier thresholds
Phase 1: Baseline and instrumentation. Milestones: inventory current features, thresholds, labels, and traffic slices; add logging for score distributions, confidence, downstream outcome, latency, and escalation rate; define gold and shadow evaluation sets segmented by domain, language, prompt length, ambiguity, and safety class. Verification: stable data pipeline, reproducible offline metrics, no missing critical telemetry, baseline precision/recall/calibration documented. Rollback: disable new logging fields if overhead spikes; revert to prior metric definitions if dashboards drift. Extension points: add new features, per-segment thresholds, cost-aware objective, calibration layer.
Phase 2: Threshold analysis and candidate policies. Milestones: compute ROC/PR and cost curves; identify under- and over-routing regions; propose global threshold changes and segmented thresholds by task family or confidence band; define policy guardrails for minimum safe recall and maximum expensive-route rate. Verification: offline win over baseline on agreed objective, improved calibration error, no severe regressions in protected segments. Rollback: keep baseline thresholds as default; gate candidates behind config flags. Extension points: dynamic thresholds by load, user tier, or SLA.
Phase 3: Shadow deployment. Milestones: run candidate thresholds in read-only mode on live traffic; compare predicted routing decisions versus actual outcomes; inspect disagreement buckets. Verification: shadow metrics match offline directionally, disagreement review completed, no hidden skew by locale or product surface. Rollback: stop shadow job and retain logs for analysis. Extension points: active learning queue from high-disagreement samples.
Phase 4: Controlled rollout. Milestones: enable to small traffic percentage, then ramp gradually by segment; monitor quality, latency, cost, escalation, abandonment, and incident rate. Verification: predeclared success criteria met for each ramp, on-call signoff, no guardrail breach. Rollback: instant config revert to previous thresholds, freeze ramps, invalidate cached policies if needed. Extension points: auto-ramp controller, multi-armed threshold testing.
Phase 5: Continuous maintenance. Milestones: periodic recalibration, drift detection, relabeling backlog, quarterly threshold review. Verification: drift alarms tested, retraining/recalibration SLA met, postmortems feed feature updates. Rollback: revert to last known-good threshold package. Extension points: online calibration, domain-specific classifiers, uncertainty estimation.

2) Controller arbitration
Phase 1: Decision policy audit. Milestones: document current controller hierarchy, tie-break rules, fail-open/fail-closed behavior, and dependencies; enumerate all arbitration inputs such as classifier score, tool availability, policy constraints, latency budget, and user tier. Verification: complete decision table and state diagram reviewed by owners, unit tests cover current behavior. Rollback: none required beyond preserving current logic as reference. Extension points: plug-in arbitration strategies, richer context signals.
Phase 2: Policy redesign. Milestones: define explicit objective function balancing quality, latency, cost, and safety; simplify precedence rules; separate hard constraints from soft preferences; add deterministic tie-breaks and reason codes. Verification: simulation over historical traces shows fewer conflicting decisions, lower nondeterminism, and improved objective score. Rollback: retain legacy arbitrator path under feature flag. Extension points: learned arbitration ranker, segment-specific policy bundles.
Phase 3: Safety and resilience hardening. Milestones: add timeouts, dependency health checks, degraded-mode policies, and circuit breakers for unavailable routes or tools; define default route when inputs are missing or stale. Verification: chaos tests and fault injection confirm bounded latency and safe fallback under partial outages. Rollback: disable new breakers if they create false trips; revert to simple default route policy. Extension points: adaptive timeout budgets, health-weighted arbitration.
Phase 4: Experimentation and rollout. Milestones: run shadow arbitration with reason-code comparison; launch A/B test on limited traffic; review counterfactual cases where new controller differs. Verification: statistically significant improvement on primary objective, no safety or SLA regressions, support tickets stable. Rollback: feature flag off, revert precedence table, clear controller caches. Extension points: policy-as-config with validation, real-time experiment slicing.
Phase 5: Governance and maintainability. Milestones: add policy linter, approval workflow, changelog, and versioned decision tables; establish ownership and incident playbook. Verification: every policy change is reviewable, reproducible, and attributable; rollback drill passes. Rollback: pin to previous policy version. Extension points: policy simulation UI, formal verification for hard constraints.

3) Hybrid routing overrides
Phase 1: Override taxonomy and scope. Milestones: catalog manual, policy-driven, customer-tier, safety, regional, and incident-response overrides; define precedence among overrides and base routing; set TTLs and ownership for each override type. Verification: no ambiguous precedence, every override has owner, expiry, and audit fields. Rollback: remove undocumented overrides and fall back to base routing. Extension points: temporary campaign overrides, partner-specific rules.
Phase 2: Override control plane. Milestones: build or refine centralized config store, validation schema, staged publish, audit log, and dry-run preview; support scoped targeting by product, tenant, region, model family, and traffic percentage. Verification: invalid configs rejected, dry-run shows deterministic affected population, audit trail complete. Rollback: revert config version, block further publishes, restore previous snapshot. Extension points: self-service UI, approval chains, API-based automation.
Phase 3: Runtime enforcement and observability. Milestones: implement fast lookup path with low-latency caching; emit reason codes and effective-route telemetry; expose dashboards for override hit rate, affected quality, cost, and latency. Verification: negligible latency overhead, telemetry completeness, cache invalidation works, no mismatch between configured and effective routes. Rollback: bypass override layer via kill switch, flush caches, use base routing only. Extension points: hierarchical overrides, context-aware predicates.
Phase 4: Guardrails and conflict resolution. Milestones: enforce max blast radius, mandatory TTLs, conflict detector, and simulation before publish; reserve emergency override channel with stricter audit. Verification: conflicting rules blocked or resolved deterministically, emergency path tested, blast-radius limits honored. Rollback: revoke offending override version, activate emergency baseline profile. Extension points: conflict explanation engine, policy scoring for override risk.
Phase 5: Operationalization. Milestones: create runbooks for incidents, launches, and partner exceptions; schedule cleanup of expired overrides; review long-lived overrides for migration into standard policy. Verification: expired overrides auto-remove, stale-rule count trends down, incident MTTR improves with override tooling. Rollback: disable auto-cleanup if it misfires; manually restore prior version from audit log. Extension points: recommendation engine for override retirement, anomaly detection on override usage.

Cross-subsystem milestones
A) Unified metrics and goals. Define common scorecard: answer quality, safety incidents, latency, compute cost, escalation rate, route mix, override hit rate, and user satisfaction. Verification: one dashboard with drill-down by segment and subsystem.
B) Config/version management. Version thresholds, arbitration policies, and overrides together when releases are coupled. Verification: every live decision can be traced to exact versions.
C) Experiment framework. Support shadow, replay, A/B, and canary across all three subsystems. Verification: comparable sampling, reason codes, and counterfactual logging.
D) Data and labeling loop. Route difficult disagreements and override-heavy traffic into review queue. Verification: label SLA met and findings feed next threshold/policy updates.

Suggested milestone timeline
Weeks 1-2: instrumentation, policy audit, override taxonomy.
Weeks 3-4: offline analyses, redesigned arbitration policy draft, control-plane validation.
Weeks 5-6: shadow deployments for thresholds and arbitration, runtime override telemetry.
Weeks 7-8: limited canaries and A/Bs, guardrails/conflict handling, rollback drills.
Weeks 9-10: broader rollout, governance hardening, maintenance cadence.

Exit criteria for program completion
Thresholds: calibrated and improved objective with stable guardrails in production.
Arbitration: deterministic, reason-coded decisions with resilient fallback behavior.
Overrides: audited, low-latency, conflict-safe control plane with operational runbooks.
Overall: measurable gains in quality/cost/latency tradeoff, full observability, and proven rollback paths."
}
